title: The Recipe of Route 9
premise: Edmund 'Eddie' Zhou has survived three years at Ashgrove Academy by being unremarkable—until her best friend Priya vanishes the night before the spring lacrosse semifinal, leaving only a ring of keys labeled in Priya's handwriting. Following the keys through the school's locked spaces, Eddie uncovers a scholarship-fraud ring run by the beloved athletic director, one Priya was about to expose, and discovers Eddie's own admission was bought by a benefactor with strings attached. When the ring tries to frame Priya for the thefts she was documenting, Eddie must testify publicly—sacrificing her scholarship, her anonymity, and Priya's forgiveness—before the final game, where the truth comes out in front of the whole school and Priya, found alive and hiding with evidence, walks onto the field to stand beside her.
about_author: Ansel Sandoval is a former boarding school scholarship kid who now teaches creative writing at a community college in upstate New York. 'The Recipe of Route 9' was inspired by the diner off the highway where he once wrote his own college application essay.

chapters.title: The Counting Habit
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Establishes Eddie's ritual: crossing off days to graduation in a diner off Route 9, invisible by design at Ashgrove. Her friendship with loud, brilliant Priya is her one indulgence. Beat: contentment that the reader can feel is about to break.

chapters.title: Forty-Three Days
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Semifinal week begins; Priya is distracted, secretive, snapping at Eddie and asking odd questions about financial aid paperwork. Eddie assumes stress. Beat: first hairline crack, disguised as ordinary friendship friction.

chapters.title: The Ring of Keys
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Priya misses the semifinal. By midnight, Eddie finds Priya's backpack in the boathouse with her phone dead and a ring of seven keys, each taped with a label: 'boiler,' 'archive,' 'Route 9.' Beat: dread arriving quietly.

chapters.title: Missing Persons Are Complicated
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Eddie and Priya (flashback). Police call it a runaway; the school agrees suspiciously fast. Eddie remembers Priya's last week through flashback—photocopying documents, a confrontation with Athletic Director Voss. Beat: the reader knows what Eddie half-suspects.

chapters.title: Key One: The Boiler Room
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. First key opens a crawlspace behind the boiler where Priya stashed a duffel: printouts of scholarship ledgers showing 'donor-funded' awards routed through a shell company. Eddie's own name is in the file. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: What My Admission Cost
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV, with a phone call to her mother. Eddie learns her 'merit' scholarship came from the same shell company—she was bought, like inventory. Shame wars with anger. Beat: identity theme lands; invisibility was never her own achievement.

chapters.title: Key Two: The Archive
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. The school archive holds ten years of doctored transcripts—star athletes' grades inflated to keep them eligible, their families billed later. Voss catches her inside but lets her go, too smoothly. Beat: the hunter knows the hunted.

chapters.title: The Benefactor's Letter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, flashback to three weeks earlier. Priya found the scheme, then found the benefactor's letters: a wealthy alum funding Voss, and a condition that Eddie be admitted—Priya's own application was rejected to make room. Beat: Priya's secret, and her guilt, revealed to the reader.

chapters.title: Everyone Has a Recipe
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Eddie interrogates the diner's owner, Route 9 fixture Marisol, who once 'fixed' paperwork for Ashgrove kids and recognizes the shell company. Marisol warns her: 'Everyone here has a recipe. Yours just got read aloud.' Beat: ally gained, stakes named.

chapters.title: Key Three: The Boathouse Loft
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. A key opens a hidden loft with Priya's sleeping bag, food, and a notebook: Priya wasn't taken—she ran, planning to gather evidence and return before graduation. Last entry: 'If I don't come back, tell Eddie the truth about Route 9.' Beat: relief and hurt in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Friend I Didn't Interrogate
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Eddie realizes Priya knew about the bought admission and said nothing—protecting her, or pitying her. A bitter fight with Priya's absence. Beat: midpoint reversal; the missing friend becomes the friend who lied.

chapters.title: Key Four: Voss's Office
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Riskiest break-in: Voss's office, where Eddie photographs the current ledger and finds a termination letter for Priya's 'withdrawal'—backdated to before she vanished. Someone is erasing her. Beat: danger becomes mortal.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The school announces Priya embezzled donor funds; her locker is emptied, her name scrubbed from the team roster. Eddie's stolen photos are her only counterweight—and now she's being watched. Beat: public narrative turns against the victim.

chapters.title: Key Five: The Chapel Crypt
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. A key opens a crypt under the old chapel: the shell company's original paperwork, and the benefactor's name—Headmaster Whitfield. The rot goes to the top. Beat: the conspiracy's true scale revealed.

chapters.title: Route 9, Mile Marker 31
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, present tense. Priya, hiding at Marisol's cousin's motel, is running out of money and courage, drafting a confession she's afraid no one will believe. She sees Eddie's missing-person flyer with her own face on it. Beat: the two storylines nearly touch.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Voss offers a deal: return the keys, stay quiet, keep the scholarship and the diploma. Eddie, who has spent the book counting the cost of everything, must decide what survival is worth. Beat: the theme made explicit; temptation at its strongest.

chapters.title: Key Six: The Diner Booth
chapters.summary: Eddie and Priya's POV, converging. Eddie leaves a note in the diner's classifieds code Marisol taught her. Priya reads it and comes in the back door at 2 a.m. The reunion is not warm—it's an accounting. Beat: friendship confronted honestly before it can be repaired.

chapters.title: Key Seven: The Trophy Case
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The last key opens the trophy case's false back, where Whitfield keeps the master ledger and recorded 'donor calls.' They photograph everything, then trip an alarm. Beat: the evidence is won; the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Championship day. Whitfield suspends Eddie hours before the final, citing the break-in. Eddie chooses to speak at halftime in front of the whole school—parents, press, the board—reading from the ledger. Beat: climax; invisibility traded for voice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Priya walks onto the field with the crypt documents; Marisol arrives with the diner's copies; the board can't unsee it. Whitfield and Voss are escorted out as the game resumes without them. Beat: catharsis, but victory feels raw, not clean.

chapters.title: What the Scholarship Didn't Cover
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Fallout: Eddie's funding is void, graduation uncertain; Priya's name cleared but her senior year scarred. They sit in the diner doing the math on what Eddie owes and what she'll do—community college, a job, the long way. Beat: the price of survival, paid honestly.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Eddie's POV. Graduation day, invited back by the new interim head. Eddie crosses off the last day—but starts a new count instead: days since she told the truth. Priya hands her a new key, to the diner's back door. Beat: identity rebuilt, friendship earned, future open.
